Lessons.Title: Using Graphs to Find Average Rate of Change
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: use two points on a function graph to compute average rate of change as (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a), interpret positive/negative/zero rates and attend to context-specific units. Original first-party Edulytiks lesson based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 7, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/7/preparation.html and source student activities at https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/7/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Official Addressing HSF-IF.B.6 and Building Towards HSF-IF.B.6.

Original hypothetical temperature-monitoring data (hours since 4 PM, degrees Celsius): (0,12),(2,4),(6,−2). Between 4 and 6 PM average rate is (4−12)/(2−0)=−4°C/hour. Between 6 and 10 PM average rate is (−2−4)/(6−2)=−6/4=−1.5°C/hour. The total temperature change is different from per-hour rate; the earlier interval cools faster even though the second interval spans four hours.

Another independent context is a water tank: measured volume V(1)=90 litres and V(5)=50 litres. Over 1–5 minutes, the secant slope equals (50−90)/(5−1)=−10 litres/minute, describing an average net decrease, not a claim that loss happened at exactly that instantaneous rate.

Student task: sketch both situations with axes/units, determine slopes of secant lines, compare rates when time intervals have different lengths, and critique a claim that the larger absolute temperature change implies faster cooling. State that an average rate does not reveal all intermediate changes.

Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for correct endpoint readings, signed Δoutput/Δinput arithmetic, units and direction interpretation, and critical rate comparison with limitations. A graph read from a teacher/student source is not reproduced as publisher artwork.

KeyConcepts.Title: Average rate of change
KeyConcepts.Definition: Change in function value divided by change in input over a specified interval.

KeyConcepts.Title: Secant slope
KeyConcepts.Definition: The average rate is slope of the line through the two endpoint graph points.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Report the endpoint coordinates and units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Sign and units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Positive, negative and zero slopes mean net rise, drop or no change per unit input.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A negative rate is not automatically a negative observed quantity.
KeyConcepts.Example: Temperature can remain above zero while its rate is negative.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare two cooling intervals
WorkedExamples.Question: T(0)=12,T(2)=4,T(6)=−2, with hours since4PM.
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: The first interval is faster cooling in magnitude.
WorkedExamples.Check: Rates use distinct durations, not raw total drops.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find water tank rate
WorkedExamples.Question: V(1)=90L, V(5)=50L. Find average rate.
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: Interpret as average net loss, without assuming uniform flow every instant.
WorkedExamples.Check: Four minutes times −10 L/min gives −40 litres.

WorkedExamples.Title: Distinguish net change from slope
WorkedExamples.Question: The temperature falls 6°C over4h; is the rate −6°C/h?
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: Average rate divides by elapsed time4h.
A rate of −6°C/h would imply −24°C over4h under constant change, inconsistent with endpoints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Multiplying true rate by four reproduces net −6°C.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using total change as average rate
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It omits the input interval duration.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Divide output change by input change.
Use consistent (b−a) in numerator and denominator.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Interpreting average rate as exactly constant every second
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Endpoints do not determine the path between them.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use average or secant, not instantaneous claims.

SummaryPoints: Average rate of change equals secant slope between endpoints.
Signed slopes and units matter for comparison.
4–6PM cools faster than 6–10PM in the fictional temperature record.
A teacher scores reasoning, graph choice and interpretation.
